text:
oliver: quick idea — instead of a bunch of ad-hoc shims in runtime, what if we build a small "translator-orchestrator" service that sits in front of the runtime and handles request translation (v1->v2), header mapping, and rollout routing?

sarah: curious — how is this different from a central gateway? sounds similar.

oliver: good q. gateway does many cross-cutting things and is heavy; translator would be purpose-built and version-aware: minimal func, fast mappings, per-tenant rules. can be deployed either as central service or as per-cluster sidecar.

raj: main tradeoff I see: sidecar = per-node isolation, no cross-tenant blast radius, easier local caching. central = single place to update mappings and telemetry, simpler rollout. perf-wise sidecar avoids extra network hop if colocated.

kate: also ops: central needs HA, shards, and more CPU. sidecars multiply deployment objects and complicate upgrades. which do we expect to iterate more often — mappings or infra? my bet mappings will change more.

oliver: mappings iterate fast. plan A: start central translator to get feature parity + telemetry, then evaluate sidecar for perf-critical tenants. central lets us dark-launch translation rules.

raj: two BIG gotchas: 1) auth/identity — we must preserve original auth contexts for billing/quotas; 2) KV cache invalidation — prefix caching in runtime might vary between v1 and v2 semantics. need mapping hooks.

oliver: agreed. auth: translator should pass through original token and add an X-Compat-Version header. no token exchange. quotas still counted at runtime. translator only rewrites request body/headers.

kate: about cache — we should have translator compute a stable cache key translation and emit a cache-key header for runtime to respect. runtime team: can we read and prefer X-Compat-Cache-Key if present? (@infra-bot tagging runtime for feasibility)

infra-bot: @kate asked runtime teams. quick note: adding a preferential header is low-risk; will need a flag gate for rollout. perf cost: negligible.

oliver: rollout plan sketch:
- implement central translator behind feature flag
- dark-launch with 0% routing (record-only mapping errors, latency) for 1 week
- canary traffic 1% -> 10% over 2 weeks with automatic rollback on error rate or p50 latency regressions > 15%
- if stable, offer a sidecar image for tenant opt-in for low-latency paths

raj: tests: unit mapping tests, end-to-end with synthetic traffic, and a small tenant beta. also fuzz old clients to catch malformed inputs. we should also add a migration metric: "compat_translation_error_v1_to_v2" and a per-tenant mapping latency histogram.

kate: deprecation policy note: need an explicit timeline per API surface. translator should emit a warning header to clients so SDKs can surface deprecation notices. also log tenant-level usage of old shapes weekly.

oliver: final thought: keep translator stateless; any stateful per-tenant rules come from a config service (versioned). this makes rolling back trivial.

raj: +1. can we sketch a small RFC that includes schema examples, metrics, and runbook for rollback? I'll draft if others agree.

sarah: agree, please include sample mapping for streaming vs chunked responses — that's a known tricky bit.

oliver: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
